Mayson.summary: The most active person on the roster and the one carrying the most risk. Mayson appears in all 14 active client chats, routes escalations nobody else routes, and is repeatedly described by the client analysts as the only reason some accounts get answered at all. But he closed zero commitments this week against 32 overdue, and two patterns turned harmful. First, he ran an uncoordinated Facebook-access campaign: the identical message 'do you have a facebook account available to use?' went to at least six clients on 2026-09-16 alone, including one two days after she warned she might leave, one 21 days post-surgery, and one who had already given ALTR that access in June. Second, and more seriously, he solicited live credentials and 2FA codes directly in group chats that contain outsourced vendor accounts. In Sarah Lloyd's chat he asked for a Snapchat 2FA code 3 hours 48 minutes after Mica posted a security advisory into that same thread telling the client never to send codes to anyone, including ALTR. He is not the cause of the credential policy gap, but he is its most frequent trigger, and that needs to stop this week.
strengths: Present in all 14 active chats and the single most responsive ALTR voice on Sarah Lloyd, Lauren Blake and Vale; the analysts for those accounts independently called him 'the engine' and 'the best worker on the account'.
Does the internal escalation work nobody else does — four escalations on Liza's behalf in 16 days, one of them pre-emptive, and he chased Vivek on Barbara's account twice in twenty minutes.
Fast and warm when he does engage: Barbara got a call offer within 38 minutes of her retention warning.
coaching_flags: CREDENTIAL SOLICITATION — the priority item. Asked for and received passwords and live 2FA codes in group chats across Sarah Lloyd, Lauren Blake, Sarah and Haileigh. Must move to role-based access and 1:1 channels immediately.
Opens workstreams and never closes them: the 'trial reels' call was offered to at least seven clients and held with none of them, in several cases 11-14 days past its own proposed date.
The 2026-09-16 Facebook campaign went to six clients with no context, no stated purpose, and no coordination against access ALTR already held.
Asks clients for new assets while their own direct questions sit unanswered — explicit in Vale, Lilia, Shayna and Sarah Lloyd.
Zero commitments closed this week against 32 overdue.

Stephski.summary: Best process week of the quarter on effort and cadence, undermined by two control failures. She restored the pre-invoice OnlyFans-withdrawal heads-up across the roster and the effect is measurable and large: Amber Haze paid in 2 hours 1 minute, Shayna in 4 hours 36 minutes, Vale and Lauren Blake inside a day — against six days on the one cycle where the reminder was skipped. That practice should be made standard policy. Against that: she shipped another change of receiving-account details — the fourth to sixth change depending on the client, and the second time in ten weeks it moved a client off an account that was working — and she still does not confirm in writing when money arrives. Multiple clients are now several cycles deep with no receipt ever acknowledged, and two overpayments have gone uncaught. The one material error this week was Barbara's invoice, understated by $1,683.12; she caught it and disclosed it herself with full arithmetic, which is the right behaviour and should be said out loud.
strengths: Invented and then restored the pre-invoice withdrawal reminder, the single highest-leverage billing practice ALTR has: payment turnaround collapsed from days to hours on every account where it ran.
Self-disclosed her own $1,683.12 under-invoice to Barbara with the full arithmetic rather than quietly re-billing.
Invoices went out on cadence across the roster; turned Sarah's referral-tracking request around in four hours, closing the root cause of three consecutive late invoices.
Warm, human register that clients respond to — Haileigh's warmest exchange in months was with her.
coaching_flags: Does not confirm receipt in writing. Haileigh is three cycles unconfirmed, Vale three consecutive payments, Mila five invoices with two receipts ever. Two client overpayments went uncaught as a direct result.
Banking details have now changed 4-6 times per client in under twelve months, twice announced as a clause inside an invoice message rather than standalone and in advance.
The 'to avoid any pausing in work' clause is going to clients who have never missed a payment — Lilia, Sarah Lloyd, Barbara and Haileigh all received it this week.
Chases the newest invoice while the oldest ages out: Alanna's invoice #2 is 10 days past term and unmentioned for 13 days while #3 was chased the day after issue.

Michelle.summary: The weekly DMCA leak-removal report stopped everywhere at once. It last ran on 2026-09-08 across Amber Haze, Barbara, Haileigh, Sarah Lloyd and Sarah, and on 2026-09-01 for Lauryn — and then did not run again in any chat. That report is the one ALTR deliverable multiple clients thank us for unprompted and never have to chase; it had unbroken streaks of eight, nine, ten, eleven and twelve weeks depending on the account. It broke in Shayna's chat the week she was thanked for it, in Barbara's the week she threatened to leave, in Alex Paige Moore's the week she resigned, and in Amber Haze's the week she asked ALTR to prove it does any work. Because it stopped simultaneously across ten chats rather than degrading in one, this reads as an availability or capacity event rather than ten separate lapses — worth establishing what happened before it is treated as a performance issue. Separately and independently of the cadence break, she re-posted a client's live plaintext Instagram password back into Liza's 20-person group chat on 2026-09-12, having copied it out of the scrollback.
strengths: Until 2026-09-08 she ran the most reliable service line in the agency — five unbroken multi-month cadences across different clients, delivered without ever being reminded.
The leak report is the single most-thanked ALTR deliverable across the whole roster.
coaching_flags: AVAILABILITY — the weekly leak report stopped in ten chats simultaneously after 2026-09-08 and has not resumed. Establish cause before treating as performance.
Re-posted a client's live plaintext Instagram password into a 20-person group chat on 2026-09-12, and asked the client to troubleshoot an account ALTR had already been told was deleted.

Mica Vecco.summary: The standout of the week, and by some distance the best ratio on the roster: 6 commitments kept against 2 overdue across 10 clients. On 2026-09-17 she pushed an unprompted Instagram security advisory into client chats across the roster, ending with 'Please do not send your backup codes to anyone, including our team.' Every single client analyst that saw it called it out as the best proactive work on their account — and she wrote it unasked, in the same week three clients posted live passwords and 2FA codes into group chats. It is a direct, unrequested fix to the agency's largest open risk and it should be made standard onboarding policy immediately. Her reel-inspo cadence also recovered sharply: an 11-link drop for Amber Haze and Mila, the largest ever and the first full one in 33 days, and resumed weekly drops for Alex Paige Moore, Sarah Lloyd and Haileigh. Two real coaching notes remain, both about targeting rather than effort: on Alanna she sent eleven other people's reels to a creator doing 32M views, repeating the exact error that drew that client's only-ever pushback, and on Vale she opened with 'how is everything going?', ignored the answer 'Been struggling to get new followers', and sent a mass template.
